record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.context_brief: Genericity in string and M-theory cosmology
record.original_question: For the stable solutions obtained in the preceding string and M-theory asymptotic problems, what do full inhomogeneous generic perturbations look like, and what features must a generic analytic cosmological solution share with those stable solutions?

evidence.quote:
2.6 Genericity issues in string and M-theory cosmology
For stable solutions found in the previous two problems, a genericity analysis to the full inhomogeneous perturbations may be applied. One expects in this way to discover what any generic solution sharing such characteristics will look like, at least for the analytic case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider cosmological solutions of the low-energy effective field equations arising from string theory and M-theory, formulated as systems of nonlinear PDEs on a spacetime manifold of the form M = R x Sigma (with Sigma a spatial slice of suitable dimension determined by the theory) coupled to scalar (dilaton/moduli) and antisymmetric form fields. Suppose that within the class of spatially homogeneous cosmological models for such systems one has identified a family of asymptotic solutions near a singular epoch (e.g. as proper time t tends to 0 or to infinity) that are stable in the sense that homogeneous perturbations decay or remain bounded relative to the background.

The problem is the following:

(a) For each such stable homogeneous asymptotic solution, analyze the full inhomogeneous perturbation problem: linearize the field equations about the background, allowing perturbations that depend on all spatial coordinates as well as time, and determine the asymptotic behavior, gauge-invariant modes, and stability properties of these inhomogeneous perturbations near the singular epoch.

(b) Using this analysis, characterize the properties that every generic analytic cosmological solution of the underlying string/M-theory effective equations, lying in a neighborhood of the chosen stable background, must share with that background. In particular, identify the asymptotic invariants (such as Kasner-type exponents, dilaton velocities, scaling of form-field energies, and dependence on the maximal number of free analytic functions of the spatial coordinates) that any generic analytic solution must exhibit.

Provide such a genericity description for the stable asymptotic solutions of the string and M-theory cosmological systems.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this genericity question for stable string/M-theory cosmological backgrounds was located. Related work on BKL-type analyses and cosmological billiards in supergravity addresses generic singular behavior but does not provide a complete genericity classification for the stable asymptotic solutions in question. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Cosmological Billiards (Damour, Henneaux, Nicolai)
status_evidence.snippet: Review of BKL-type generic asymptotic behavior in supergravity/string cosmology near spacelike singularities, leaving full genericity for stable backgrounds open.
status_evidence.claim: General genericity analysis for stable string/M-theory cosmological backgrounds with inhomogeneous perturbations remains incomplete.
